title: Brooklyn Bridge Park, Pier 1
text: The postcard view: {n} landmarks, with the Brooklyn Bridge close by and the Statue of Liberty down the harbor.

title: Mount Olivet Cemetery
text: The most landmarks visible from any public spot in the model: {n} of 16, from a hillside {elev} feet above sea level in Maspeth. Only the Unisphere is out of sight.

title: Highland Park
text: The glaciers left a ridge along the Brooklyn–Queens border. From the hilltop by the old Ridgewood Reservoir, {n} of the 16 are in view across the flats below.

title: Times Square
text: In the middle of the skyline, you can't see any of it. From the bowtie, none of the 16 is visible: the towers that make Times Square also wall it in.

title: Washington Square
text: Fifth Avenue starts at the arch and runs straight at the Empire State Building, {esb_mi} miles north. On the map, the avenue lights up like a beam.

title: Sunset Park
text: From the park's hilltop, {elev} feet up, {n} landmarks across the harbor and the city.

title: Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge
text: Out on the West Pond trail, nothing stands between the marsh and the skyline: {n} landmarks, out to the {far_name}, {far_mi} miles away.

title: Wards Island
text: Manhattan's best view is off the main island: {n} landmarks, with the Hell Gate Bridge's arch next door.

title: Alice Austen House lawn
text: Staten Island's front porch on the Narrows: {n} landmarks, from the Verrazzano to the Midtown towers.

title: Ferry Point Park
text: The Bronx sees the least of any borough, but this park near where the East River opens into Long Island Sound takes in {n} landmarks.

title: Calvary Cemetery
text: Midtown rising behind the headstones, a view familiar from the movies: {n} landmarks.

title: Domino Park
text: From the old sugar refinery's waterfront, {n} landmarks across the East River.

title: The Empire State's longest reach
text: The farthest public ground in the city that still sees the Empire State Building: Charleston, Staten Island, {esb_mi} miles away.
